title: FORD TOWN FUN FEST 2026
full_story:
The location for the festival is in front of the Flora Public Library and Food trucks will be set up on East 2nd Street.

The event starts with a Cruise in Friday from 5 pm, starting at the parking lot of Beck’s Auto Sales with dash plaques to the first 100 entries.  The car show is open to any make or model of car.  They will be cruising through town and past Heritage Woods so the residents can look at the vehicles.  Food trucks inflatables and family yard games will be available at Library Park from 5 to 8 pm, and Just for Spite Unplugged will be playing from 6 to 9 pm.

Saturday the Clay County Cruisers will have a Car Show with registration from 9 until Noon.  The car show registration is $15 and there will be awards for the top 75 plus 5 specialty awards.  For Car show information call 618-676-4005, 618-662-5646 or 618-676-7732.  Dash plaques will be given to the first 100 entrants.  Craft and food vendors, inflatables, and games will also open at 9 am.  There are also commemorative T-shirts available for $20.

At noon the craft brew and chili cookoff sampling will begin and the dunking booth will open.  Car show awards are at 3 pm and craft beer and chili judging will begin at 4 pm.  So far there are 7 entries in the craft brew contest and 6 entries in the Chili Cookoff, with entries still being taken.  The winner of the Chili Cookoff will win a $100 gift card and have their name engraved on the Chili Cookoff Plaque in City Hall.  For more information call Arriel at the Chamber Office at 618-662-5646.

title: FLORA HIGH SCHOOL HOMECOMING
full_story:
Flora High School is gearing up for Homecoming week which will start with Dress up days next Monday.

Monday, September 21st will be Movie Star Monday, where students will dress as their favorite movie star.  Tuesday, September 22nd will be Something you Can’t Wear Anywhere Else day.  Wednesday, September 23rd will be Color War Day, Seniors will wear black, Juniors will wear yellow, Sophomores will wear Red, and Freshmen will wear Green.  Faculty will be dressed in Blue.  Thursday, September 24th will be Dolly Parton Day and Pink Out Day. and Friday, September 25th will be Crazy Orange and Blue Day.

The Homecoming Parade will be held Wednesday night, September 23rd beginning at 7:30 pm through downtown Flora.  The parade will start at the Depot with line up at 7, and end at the corner of North Avenue and Mill Street.  Class Competitions will then be held on Dancey Field at 8 with the bonfire to follow.

Friday night, September 25th, at 7 pm will be the Homecoming Football game at Dancey Field, against the Eldorado Eagles with the Homecoming court announced during half time of the game.

The student body has chosen the Queen candidates of Myra Sloan, Marli Myers, Qynlin Brown, Danica Conklin and Rosalyn Stanford.  King Candidates are Guy Arnold, Rylan Billingsly, Kehlin Crawford, Brennan O’Donnell, and Kormik Massie.  The Junior Class attendants are Morgan Irmen, Mylea Jones, Kennedy Zimmerman, Tyler Earnst, Braxton Oestrich, and Ashton Williams.  The Sophomores Class attendants are Vayda Kohn and Carson Smith.  The Freshmen Class Attendants are Halle Patridge and Sawyer Murbarger.

The coronation of the King and Queen will be held Saturday night, September 26th in the FHS Gym.  Dance opens at 7 for students, parents are welcome to enter at 7:15, coronation begins at 7:30 and dance is from 8 to 10 pm.

title: PLUMMER RECOGNIZED
full_story:
State Senator Jason Plummer has been recognized by the National Federation of Independent Business (NFIB) with its 2026 Guardian of Small Business Award for his strong voting record and continued advocacy on behalf of Illinois small businesses.

The Guardian of Small Business Award recognizes leaders who stand up for and advocate on behalf of small businesses.  Senator Plummer was selected for the award by a panel of small business owners from across the state.

“I’m humbled to receive this recognition from NFIB, but more importantly, it’s a reminder of how much work still needs to be done to make Illinois a better place to start and grow a business,” said Senator Plummer.  “Small businesses create the most jobs, invest in our communities and keep our local economies moving, yet they are too often overlooked in Springfield.  I’ll continue working to make sure their concerns are heard and to push back against policies that make it harder to do business and provide quality jobs for Illinois families.”

Plummer earned a 100 percent voting record from NFIB during the 2025-2026 legislative session.  Members of the NFIB Illinois Leadership Council, which is made up of small business owners from across the state, selected Plummer for the award based on his strong record of standing up for Illinois small businesses.

“Senator Plummer’s knowledge of business issues makes him an effective advocate for Main Street businesses,” said NFIB Illinois State Director Noah Finley.  “Small business owners know he will stand up for their interests in Springfield, even when it means bucking powerful interest groups.”

title: FARM BILL
full_story:
As the Senate returns for its work session this week, a proposed farm bill has another shot at moving forward.

Although the legislation failed to advance in the Senate Ag Committee before senators’ August recess, chairman John Boozman, said he hopes to bring the bill back for markup this week.  As of press time, the markup had not been scheduled.

The proposed Senate farm bill failed 10-11 along party lines, with two Republican committee members; Mitch McConnell, and Tommy Tuberville, both absent from the meeting.

However, reports indicate McConnell could return to the Capitol during the Senate’s work period after a three-month medical-related absence.

Passing a modernized five-year farm bill remains a top priority for Illinois Farm Bureau as farmers continue to deal with ag economy challenges.  The 2018 farm bill expired in 2023, and has since been extended several times by Congress.  The current extension will expire September 30th.

The House passed its version of a farm bill in April, marking the first time a farm bill passed the House floor since 2018.  The legislation’s failure in the Senate Ag Committee is largely attributed to deep divides over nutrition aid.

The Senate farm bill, the Agricultural Act of 2026, modernizes essential farm programs, authorizes year-round sales of E15 to strengthen markets for American agriculture and includes measures to help reduce input cost volatility.

Despite the bipartisan amendment process, the bill failed to advance out of committee during the markup due to partisan gridlock over the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) state cost share.  Boozman recessed the committee allowing him to bring the members back to consider the legislation when the Senate returned.

“Farm Bureau believes Chairman Boozman’s farm bill includes important support for farm families across the country, and the Senate Agriculture Committee should quickly advance this bill out of markup in a bipartisan manner,” American Farm Bureau Federation staff wrote in a recent Farm Bureau Intel article.

The Senate bill provides support for farm families including improved access to credit, expanded investments in specialty crops, increased transparency in fertilizer markets and enhanced research and conservation programs.

Both the House and Senate bills build upon last year’s reconciliation bill that invested $66 billion in farm programs and strengthened parts of the farm safety net, but reconciliation rules left major farm bill titles unfinished.

“The Senate Agriculture Committee’s farm bill is strong legislation that delivers much-needed certainty and support for America’s farmers and ranchers,” according to the Farm Bureau Intel.  “Congress must still address remaining priorities not currently in this farm bill draft, including protecting interstate commerce from a patchwork of state laws and providing economic assistance to producers facing record-high production expenses and historic inflation.  Together, these actions will strengthen the farm economy, support rural communities and reinforce agriculture’s role in the nation’s food, energy and national security.”

If the Senate Ag Committee advances the legislation, the full Senate would then need to approve the bill.  At that point, the legislation would move to a conference committee, which is a joint body of members from both the House and Senate appointed to reconcile differences between the two versions into a single bill that can be passed by both chambers without further amendment.

title: ILLINOIS SPEED AWARENESS DAY
full_story:
Nearly 4,000 speeding citations were issued and hundreds of arrests were made during the 2026 Illinois Speed Awareness Day, according to the Illinois Association of Chiefs of Police.

Launched by the ILACP in 2016, Illinois Speed Awareness Day is a traffic safety initiative focused on reducing speeding and raising awareness about the dangers of excessive speed.

This year, 160 law enforcement agencies registered to participate.  Officers and deputies worked a combined 5,153 hours.  A total of 3,795 speeding citations and 1,863 speeding warnings were issued.

In addition, there were 18 alcohol-related DUI arrests, 17 drug-related DUI arrests, 211 traffic arrests and 140 other arrests, for a total of 386 arrests.

While the initiative focuses on speeding, officers encountered other criminal activity during their patrols.

“There is no acceptable level of speeding,” ILACP President Eric Barden said.  “By working together we share a common goal: reducing crashes, preventing injuries and most importantly, saving lives.”

title: FCC SENIOR CITIZENS DAY
full_story:
Frontier Community College will host a Senior Citizen’s Day event on Friday, September 25th, in West Hall, rooms 103, 104 and 105.

The event is designed to provide helpful information, resources, and support for senior citizens.  The morning will feature presentations from local professionals on topics including financial estate planning, resiliency, hospital resources, healthy meals, adult education, and tutoring opportunities.

Registration and breakfast will begin at 8 am, followed by opening remarks at 8:30 am from Frontier Community College President Dr. Sharmila Kakac and Lori Noe, Director of Learning Commons.

Luke Harl, Financial Advisor with FNB Financial, will present “Financial Estate Planning for Senior Citizens” from 9 to 9:30.  Following a short break, Dana Taylor, Chief Operating Officer at Fairfield Memorial Hospital, will speak on “Resiliency Through Life Challenges” from 9:45 to 10:05.  Taylor will also share information about specialized resources and services available at Fairfield Memorial Hospital.

Additional sessions will include guided breathing imagery provided by Fairfield Memorial Hospital, “Healthy Snacks – Healthy Meals” with Whitney Buckles of Fairfield Memorial Hospital, and “Adult Education – Tutoring Opportunities” with Sharis Wilson, Director of Literacy and Adult Education Operations.

The event will conclude with door prizes and adjournment from 11:30 to noon.  A tour of Learning Commons in Cox Hall will be offered afterward.  During the tour, attendees can learn more about the accommodations and services available to senior citizens upon request.

Advance registration is required to attend.  To register, call Frontier Community College at 618-842-3711.

title: PORK RECALLED
full_story:
Two companies have recalled more than 1,500 pounds of imported pork products from Italy over listeria contamination concerns, federal regulators announced Sunday.

New Jersey-based Ferrarini USA and Florida-based Prime Line Distributors recalled cardboard cases of vacuum-packed ready-to-eat pork products.

The products, dry-cured pork jowl, were produced on May 21st, imported into the United States throughout July and have best-by dates of May 16th, 2027, with lot code 263311US, the US Food Safety and Inspection Service said.

Ferrani USA’s products were shipped to food service and retail locations in eight states, including Illinois, California, Florida, Idaho, Michigan, New Jersey, New York and Texas, officials said.  Prime Line Distributors’ products were only shipped to locations in Florida.

The recall has been designated as a Class 1, the most serious classification, meaning there is a reasonable probability that use of the product will cause “serious, adverse health consequences or death,” according to the FSIS.

Officials warned that consumption of the products can “cause listeriosis, a serious infection that primarily affects older adults, persons with weakened immune systems, and pregnant women and their newborns.”

Listeriosis symptoms typically begin within two weeks after consuming contaminated food and can include fever, headache, stiff neck, confusion, loss of balance, seizures and flu-like symptoms such as muscle aches and fatigue, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

The recall was initiated after a sample of the product tested positive for listeria during “routine import reinspection testing,” the FSIS confirmed.  No illnesses have been reported so far in connection with the recalled product, and customers are advised to throw them away or return them to the place of purchase.

For questions, consumers can contact Ferrarini USA at 818-256-1622 or [email protected].  Prime Line Distributors can be reached at 954-925-4500 or [email protected].
